Nationwide Strike Brings Sri Lanka’s Economy to Standstill

COLOMBO – A sweeping general strike has brought much of Sri Lanka’s economic activity to a halt, as workers from transport, manufacturing, education, and health sectors collectively downed tools on Wednesday. The action, called by the United Labour Federation (ULF) in response to proposed pension reforms and rising living costs, has led to widespread disruption in cities and rural areas alike.

Public and private buses operated by Lankaride and other firms were parked at depots across the country, leaving commuters stranded and roads unusually quiet during morning rush hour. At Colombo’s main railway station, only a handful of trains ran, with most services cancelled as railway staff joined the strike.

Hospitals in several districts reported skeleton staffing, with only emergency care available. “We are running on a minimum team to handle urgent cases, but routine clinics and surgeries have been postponed,” said Dr. Sahan Wickramasinghe, director at Galle General Hospital.

Factories in the Katunayake and Biyagama export processing zones were shuttered, affecting garment and electronics exports. The Chamber of Manufacturers estimated that daily losses to the sector could exceed 1.2 billion rupees if the shutdown continues. “Every hour counts for exporters. We urge all parties to resolve differences swiftly,” said Nalin Perera, the Chamber’s spokesperson.

Schools remained closed in most provinces as teachers and administrative staff participated in the strike. Parents expressed concern over the disruption to education, with final-term exams scheduled for next week.

Government officials have called for dialogue. “We respect the right to protest, but essential services must be maintained,” said Labour Minister Chamara Fernando at a midday briefing. The ULF, however, has vowed to continue the strike until their demands are addressed.

As negotiations stall, many in Sri Lanka brace for continued uncertainty. “This is not just about wages – it’s about our future,” said union leader Rasika Jayawardene, addressing supporters at a rally in Kandy.
